newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JULY 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JULY 14.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The Simitis government is playing a juggling game between the needs of meeting convergence criteria, the desire for a peaceful home front and forthcoming municipal elections with the drafting of economic policies for the next year. The burning issues are wage increases, tax breaks for low income earners, the distribution of losses in middle and higher incomes, the imposition of a special charge on companies and changes to the job market.
--The public health sector continues to be plagued by problems as pharmacies remain shut until Wednesday and pension funds cease distributing medicines on credit as of tomorrow.

--One in two Athenians have given the thumbs down to the recently-ratified Schengen treaty and the single currency, according to a survery carried out earlier this month. However the same percentage recognised that the government's economic policies were necessary to achieve convergence and that not achieving convergence would mean "serious problems".
--A snap poll by ICAP on the Madrid agreement signed between Greece and Turkey last week shows a majority believe that Turkey had gained the most from the agreement.
--The finance ministry is working on changes to the tax regime governing cars and yachts, as well as to tax imposed on imported secondhand cars and a new recall of older generation cars.
